newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power firm, but down from Mon highs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power firm, but down from Mon highs.

text.p: Spot power prices during peak demand hours in the western U.S. retreated from Monday's high-end deals but remained firm in the mid-$40s per megawatt hour (MWh), trade sources said Tuesday.
By late Monday offers were seen as high as $60.00 per MWh in both the Northwest and Southwest as demand spurred by cold weather outstripped regional supplies of low-cost hydropower.
"I think we will see prices continuing to drop off through Saturday," said one trader, citing forecasts for warmer temperatures by this weekend.
The Northwest is also expected to see rain over the weekend.
"Loads are starting to tail off," said another trader.
In addition, a series of brief outages at coal-fired power plants in the Southwest, which contributed to Monday's market tightness, were mostly over by late Monday night.
One 330 MW unit at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant in Montana remained out of service for repairs to a cooling tower and was expected to be back on line Friday.

Bonneville Power Administration offered no power during mid-morning and evening peaks, but lowered prices for shoulder hours on Wednesday by $5.00 per MWh to $40.00 for Northwest and $41.00 for California-Oregon border (COB) deliveries.
Firm, peak electricity at COB for Wednesday was quoted at $45.00-46.50 per MWh, compared with an average near $46.00-48.00 for Tuesday.
Off-peak COB for Wednesday y was little changed at $11.00-13.00.
Wednesday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was lower at $40.00-$42.00, while off-peak was at $11.50-12.50.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Wednesday was quoted at $42.00-45.00, while off-peak was at $10.00-11.00 per MWh.
Wednesday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were quoted $40.00-44.00, while off-peak was quoted at $10.00-11.00.
Palo Verde for the balance of January was offered at $23.00, while COB was offered at $25.00.
